body_excerpt: Bulk migrate branch protections to rulesets for a repository - GitHub Changelog Skip to content Skip to sidebar / Blog Changelog Docs Customer stories Try GitHub Copilot app Attend GitHub Universe Search Changelog Docs Customer stories Attend GitHub Universe Try GitHub Copilot app Back to changelog Improvement October 20, 2026 • 1 minute read Bulk migrate branch protections to rulesets for a repository Table of Contents How it works Why migrate to rulesets? Availability Menu. Currently selected: How it works How it works Why migrate to rulesets? Availability You can now convert all branch protection rules of a repository to rulesets in a single action. This is an extension of the ability to convert a single branch protection rule to a ruleset that we released previously, now allowing for at-scale conversions. How it works Navigate to Settings → Rulesets in your repository and click Import branch protection rules . In the Review import dialog, you can: Preview the rulesets that will be created before you confirm the conversion. See which branch protection rules are already covered by an existing ruleset. Review cases where one branch protection rule produces multiple rulesets to preserve its original behavior. Choose an enforcement status (e.g., Active , Evaluate , or Disabled ) and select which rulesets to create. After you click Create rulesets , choose whether to keep or delete the original branch protection rules. Why migrate to rulesets? Rulesets offer several advantages over classic branch protections: Apply rules across multiple branches with pattern matching Layer multiple rulesets for granular policy control Manage rulesets at the organization or enterprise level Configure fine-grained bypass permissions for users, teams, and apps Availability This feature is available for all repositories where rulesets are available. Learn more about converting your branch protections to repository rulesets . Join the discussion within GitHub Community . Table of Contents

body_excerpt: GitHub package firewall in public preview - GitHub Changelog Skip to content Skip to sidebar / Blog Changelog Docs Customer stories Try GitHub Copilot app Attend GitHub Universe Search Changelog Docs Customer stories Attend GitHub Universe Try GitHub Copilot app Back to changelog Release October 20, 2026 • 1 minute read GitHub package firewall in public preview Table of Contents How it works Availability and limitations How to use it Menu. Currently selected: How it works How it works Availability and limitations How to use it An increasing number of malware attacks exploit systems at package installation time, harvesting credentials on CI/CD hosts or developer workstations without even running the package’s code. To stem this tide of attacks, GitHub is introducing a new package firewall capability. The package firewall sits between endpoints like Actions runners or coding agents and the upstream package repositories, inspecting both metadata requests and package downloads for signs of malicious activity. The package firewall is available today in public preview for all GitHub Enterprise Cloud customers, including data-resident GitHub Enterprise Cloud. How it works First, administrators set policy controls for their enterprise. The controls available today include a configurable cooldown period, checking the GitHub Advisory Database for malware or vulnerability alerts, and supply-chain checks like attestation downgrades. Then endpoints like coding agents and CI/CD hosts need configuration to use the firewall for their requests instead of pointing directly at the upstream package registries. Metadata requests for package lists as well as the actual package downloads then flow through the firewall, which evaluates them against the policy. If a package is blocked erroneously, the user can request an exception with a workflow similar to other GitHub Advanced Security features.
